title: Validate at a trusted boundary
summary: Validation checks that data follows a rule. Browser checks help the user, but a real backend must check received data too because browser code can be changed.
introduction: Validation checks that data follows a rule. Browser checks help the user, but a real backend must check received data too because browser code can be changed. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain validate at a trusted boundary
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Validation checks that data follows a rule. Browser checks help the user, but a real backend must check received data too because browser code can be changed.

blocks.code:
Page rule: quantity must be a whole number from 1 to 5
Backend rule in a real service: check the same limits before saving
This tutorial app: has no backend or accounts
blocks.title: Validate at a trusted boundary

blocks.text: The page is useful guidance, not a trusted security barrier for another service.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
List valid quantities and one invalid quantity for the rule.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not trust a value just because a browser form accepted it.
For more detail later, use this [Cybersecurity Fundamentals further reading](https://www.cisa.gov/secure-our-world).
